arxiv-2111-00565.title: Can we learn gradients by Hamiltonian Neural Networks?
arxiv-2111-00565.creator: Aleksandr Timofeev, Andrei Afonin, Yehao Liu
arxiv-2111-00565.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aleksandr Timofeev, Andrei Afonin, Yehao Liu. In this work, we propose a meta-learner based on ODE neural networks that learns gradients. This approach makes the optimizer is more flexible inducing an automatic inductive bias to the given task. Using the simplest Hamiltonian Neural Network we demonstrate that our method outperforms a meta-learner based on LSTM for an artificial task and the MNIST dataset with ReLU activations in the optimizee.

arxiv-2303-13841.title: Systematic analysis of the nuclear absorption effect on the cross section of the knockout reaction
arxiv-2303-13841.creator: Sang-In Shim, Kazuki Yoshida, Kazuyuki Ogata
arxiv-2303-13841.description: Abstract Recent studies on nucleon and alpha knockout reactions have shown that the distorted-wave impulse approximation (DWIA) is a simple and accurate method to describe these reactions. As it has been argued for decades, the nuclear absorption is one of the most important ingredients of the DWIA calculation.

arxiv-2311-12418.title: Visual Analytics for Generative Transformer Models
arxiv-2311-12418.creator: Raymond Li, Ruixin Yang, Wen Xiao
arxiv-2311-12418.description: Abstract While transformer-based models have achieved state-of-the-art results in a variety of classification and generation tasks, their black-box nature makes them challenging for interpretability. In this work, we present a novel visual analytical framework to support the analysis of transformer-based generative networks.

arxiv-2311-17909.title: Distance-coupling as an Approach to Position and Formation Control
arxiv-2311-17909.creator: Michael Napoli, Roberto Tron
arxiv-2311-17909.description: Abstract In this letter, we study the case of autonomous agents which are required to move to some new position based solely on the distance measured from predetermined reference points, or anchors. A novel approach, referred to as distance-coupling, is proposed for calculating the agent’s position exclusively from differences between squared distance measurements.

arxiv-2403-18797.title: SolderlessPCB: Reusing Electronic Components in PCB Prototyping through Detachable 3D Printed Housings Conference: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; May 11–16, 2024; Honolulu, HI, USA Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI
arxiv-2403-18797.creator: Zeyu Yan, Jiasheng Li, Zining Zhang, Huaishu Peng
arxiv-2403-18797.description: Abstract . The iterative prototyping process for printed circuit boards (PCBs) frequently employs surface-mounted device (SMD) components, which are often discarded rather than reused due to the challenges associated with desoldering, leading to unnecessary electronic waste. This paper introduces SolderlessPCB, a collection of techniques for solder-free PCB prototyping, specifically designed to promote the recycling and reuse of electronic components.

arxiv-2409-20132.title: Machine Learning in Industrial Quality Control of Glass Bottle Prints
arxiv-2409-20132.creator: Maximilian Bundscherer 1 , Thomas H. Schmitt 1 and Tobias Bocklet 1 1 Department of Computer Science, Technische Hochschule Nürnberg Georg Simon Ohm, Nuremberg, Germany { maximilian.bundscherer, thomas.schmitt, tobias.bocklet } @th-nuernberg.de
arxiv-2409-20132.description: Abstract In industrial manufacturing of glass bottles, quality control of bottle prints is necessary as numerous factors can negatively affect the printing process. Even minor defects in the bottle prints must be detected despite reflections in the glass or manufacturing-related deviations.

arxiv-2411-12545.title: When Theory Meets Experiment: What Does it Take to Accurately Predict 1 H NMR Dipolar Relaxation Rates in Neat Liquid Water from Theory?
arxiv-2411-12545.creator: Dietmar Paschek, Johanna Busch, Angel Mary Chiramel Tony, Ralf Ludwig, Anne Strate, Nore Stolte, Harald Forbert, Dominik Marx
arxiv-2411-12545.description: Abstract In this contribution, we compute the 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) relaxation rate of liquid water at ambient conditions. We are using structural and dynamical information from Coupled Cluster Molecular Dynamics (CCMD) trajectories generated at CCSD(T) electronic structure accuracy while considering also nuclear quantum effects in addition to consulting information from X-ray and neutron scattering experiments.

arxiv-2504-19693.title: Emerging Photon Jets in the Hadronic Calorimeter: A Novel Signature of Neutral Long-Lived Particles at the LHC
arxiv-2504-19693.creator: Jinheung Kim, Dongjoo Kim, Soojin Lee, Jeonghyeon Song
arxiv-2504-19693.description: Abstract We propose a novel collider signature for neutral long-lived particles (LLPs): the emerging photon jet in the hadronic calorimeter (HCAL). This signature arises when a neutral LLP decays into photons within the HCAL, producing an electromagnetic shower without associated charged tracks or energy deposits in the electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL).

arxiv-2506-05423.title: Variable Modified Newtonian Mechanics VII: Supermassive Black Hole at very High redshift
arxiv-2506-05423.creator: C. C. Wong
arxiv-2506-05423.description: Abstract Observations of Supermassive Black Hole (SMBH) at very high redshift hosted by massive galaxy provide a challenge to the SMBH and massive galaxy formation models which are predicated on the Λ ​ C ​ D ​ M \Lambda CDM model that predicts a Hubble constant currently in tension with late time observations.

arxiv-2507-16981.title: Uniqueness of stationary compatible probability measure for chains of infinite order with forbidden transitions
arxiv-2507-16981.creator: Gallesco, C. 1, Gallo, A. 2, Takahashi, D. Y. 3
arxiv-2507-16981.description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider chains of infinite order on countable state spaces with prohibited transitions. We give a set of sufficient conditions on the structure of the probability kernels of the chains to have at most one stationary probability measure compatible with the kernel.

arxiv-2508-04057.title: PAIRS: Parametric–Verified Adaptive Information Retrieval and Selection for Efficient RAG
arxiv-2508-04057.creator: Wang Chen, Guanqiang Qi, Weikang Li, Yang Li, Deguo Xia, Jizhou Huang
arxiv-2508-04057.description: Abstract Retrieval–Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a cornerstone technique for enhancing large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge. However, current RAG systems face two critical limitations: (1) they inefficiently retrieve information for every query, including simple questions that could be resolved using the LLM’s parametric knowledge alone, and (2) they risk retrieving irrelevant documents when queries contain sparse information signals.

pmc-10494923.title: Risks of Early Mortality and Associated Factors at Adult Emergency Department of Jimma University Medical Center
pmc-10494923.creator: Fikadu Abebe, Asaminew Habtamu, Abdata Workina
pmc-10494923.description: IntroductionMortality in the emergency department is still high in developing countries with resources scarce. Most of emergency department mortality occurred within the first three days; the majority of these deaths are avoidable with proper intervention. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to assess the mortality risks and therapeutic benefits of early and late death.

pmc-11445928.title: Characterization and phylogenetic analysis of the chloroplast genome in Elaeocarpus duclouxii
pmc-11445928.creator: Zhitian Du, Haoliang Hu, Xingyu Zeng, Yongle Liu, Ying Chen, Zhuoyu Chenyang, Rong Zhu, Huang Kerui
pmc-11445928.description: Elaeocarpus duclouxii, an evergreen tree species, is renowned for its fruits rich in flavonoids exhibiting potent antioxidant properties. Despite its significance, the chloroplast genome of this plant has remained unexplored until now. Our study presents the first comprehensive sequencing and analysis of the E. duclouxii chloroplast genome, revealing a circular DNA molecule of 158,148 base pairs.

pmc-11465009.title: Global research and current trends on nanotherapy in lung cancer research: a bibliometric analysis of 20 years
pmc-11465009.creator: Pooja Singh, Prabhakar Semwal, Baby Gargi, Sakshi Painuli, Michael Aschner, Khalaf F Alsharif, Haroon Khan, Rakesh Kumar Bachheti, Limenew Abate Worku
pmc-11465009.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundLung cancer ranks as one of the most rapidly growing malignancies. Which is characterized by its poor prognosis and a low survival rate due to late diagnosis and limited efficacy of conventional treatments. In recent years nanotechnology has emerged as a promising frontier in the management of lung cancer, presenting novel strategies to enhance drug administration, improve therapeutic efficiency, and mitigate side effects.

pmc-11468015.title: Biometrically measured sleep in medical students as a predictor of psychological health and academic experiences in the preclinical years
pmc-11468015.creator: Lindsay M Oberleitner, Dwayne M Baxa, Scott M Pickett, Kara E Sawarynski
pmc-11468015.description: BackgroundStudent wellness is of increasing concern in medical education. Increased rates of burnout, sleep disturbances, and psychological concerns in medical students are well documented. These concerns lead to impacts on current educational goals and may set students on a path for long-term health consequences.MethodsUndergraduate medical students were recruited to participate in a novel longitudinal wellness tracking project.

pmc-12537521.title: Effectiveness of the In-Hospital Information Technology System-Based Delirium Management Intervention Program in Medically Hospitalized Patients with Dementia: A Retrospective Case–Control Study
pmc-12537521.creator: Sin-Chen Wang, Wen-Fu Wang, Ming-Che Chang, Yu-Chun Tung, Kai-Ming Jhang
pmc-12537521.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeThis study aimed to study the effectiveness of an information technology (IT) system-based delirium management intervention program for prevention and earlier detection of delirium in medically hospitalized patients with dementia.Patients and MethodsThis was a retrospective case–control study. The study population consisted of patients aged 50–100 years who were diagnosed with dementia and hospitalized in the general wards of neurology, psychiatry, or geriatrics. The intervention group included 101 patients receiving a delirium management protocol comprising IT-supported delirium detection, multicomponent prevention, and treatment protocols.

pmc-12770041.title: Collagen dynamics in the breast cancer tumor microenvironment and therapeutic perspectives
pmc-12770041.creator: Danping Wu, Lu Liu, Ying Jiang, Zhiwen Qian, Yilan You, Xin Ning, Feng Zhang, Yida Wang, Yan Zhang
pmc-12770041.description: Breast Cancer (BC) remains one of the most prevalent malignancies among women globally, with its pathogenesis and clinical progression being profoundly regulated by the tumor microenvironment (TME). Collagen, the most abundant extracellular matrix (ECM) component, plays multifaceted roles in shaping the TME of BC.

pmc-13163521.title: Experiences of Loss and Grief Among Brazilian Frontline Healthcare Professionals During the COVID-19 Pandemic Crisis: A Grounded Theory Analysis
pmc-13163521.creator: Paola Kallyanna Guarneri Carvalho de Lima, Carlos Laranjeira, Amira Mohammed Ali, Feten Fekih-Romdhane, Murat Yıldırım, Lígia Carreira, Maria Aparecida Salci
pmc-13163521.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic exerted unprecedented pressure on healthcare professionals and systems worldwide. To manage this increased demand, hospitals extended working hours, resulting in increased strain on workers and impacting their professional well-being. Simultaneously, the numerous deaths due to illness meant that healthcare professionals did not have sufficient time to process grief, which may have led to unresolved grief and other mental health problems.

pmc-13182270.title: The role of the nucleus in the control of mitochondrial precursor proteins in yeast
pmc-13182270.creator: Kira Ritzenhofen, Stefano Rossi, Axel Mogk, Fabian den Brave
pmc-13182270.description: Mitochondria are essential organelles of eukaryotic cells, with vital roles in energy production, biosynthesis of macromolecules, and intracellular signaling. Their function depends on a complex proteome with proteins targeted to different mitochondrial sub‐compartments. Synthesis of precursors of mitochondrial proteins (mitoPREs) mostly occurs in the cytosol followed by post‐translational import.

pmc-13400363.title: Protocol for reconstructing 3D human skin equivalents on endogenous dermal matrix with optional pigmentation
pmc-13400363.creator: Khek-Chian Tham, Zhi Heng Lau, Joycelyn X.Y. Lee, Carine Bonnard
pmc-13400363.description: SummaryPrevious in vitro 3D skin models are limited by their reliance on animal-derived collagen, a poor representation of the human dermis, and low throughput. Here, we present a protocol for reconstructing 3D human skin equivalents on an endogenous dermal matrix, in 12- and 24-well format, with optional pigmentation.
